analysis.investment_thesis: Avalon Technologies fails both legs of the Magic Formula: earnings yield of ~1.5% (EBIT ₹115 Cr / EV ~₹7,568 Cr) is a fraction of the 12% minimum required, and ROCE of 12.8% falls well short of the 20%+ threshold for a "good" business. At P/E 77.8x and EV/EBITDA 52x, the market is pricing in perfection for a business with thin margins, volatile profits, and consistently negative free cash flow.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 11.3% CAGR (2020-2025) with operating income recovering to ₹115 Cr in FY25 after FY24 dip
Debt reduction underway — borrowings fell from ₹342 Cr (FY23) to ₹163 Cr (FY25), D/E now a modest 0.25x
Diversified EMS platform across aerospace, clean energy, and railways provides some end-market resilience
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~1.5% (EBIT/EV) is catastrophically low — Magic Formula requires >12%; stock is ~8x overpriced on this metric
Free cash flow has been negative for 3 consecutive years (FY23: -₹41 Cr, FY24: -₹18 Cr, FY25: -₹21 Cr) despite reported profits — working capital and capex are consuming all earnings
Net profit is wildly volatile (₹67 Cr → ₹28 Cr → ₹63 Cr in three years), suggesting no durable earnings power; operating margin at 9.6% is thin for capital-intensive EMS
red_flags: Earnings yield ~1.5% — one-tenth of Magic Formula's minimum 12% threshold
FCF negative in FY23, FY24, and FY25 despite accounting profits — earnings quality is poor
Net profit collapsed 58% from FY22 to FY24 then recovered; this is not the stable, high-ROIC business the Magic Formula targets
ROCE of 12.8% and ROE of 10.4% both below cost of capital for a mid-cap growth stock in India
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Avalon: EBIT (FY25) = ₹115 Cr; Enterprise Value = ₹7,473 Cr market cap + ₹164 Cr debt − ₹69 Cr cash = ~₹7,568 Cr. Earnings Yield = 1.52% — a disaster. ROCE of 12.8% also fails the 20%+ threshold. Both legs of the formula point to the same conclusion: this is an average-quality business trading at a premium price, the exact opposite of what the Magic Formula seeks. The EV/EBITDA of 52x prices in a decade of flawless execution that the historical financials do not support.

The business fundamentals are mediocre at best. Revenue CAGR is a respectable 11%, but it comes with razor-thin operating margins (9.6%), high capital intensity (capex rising from ₹16 Cr to ₹46 Cr over three years), and working capital that consistently consumes operating cash flow — hence negative FCF every year since FY22. The IPO (FY23 equity jump from ₹87 Cr to ₹537 Cr) raised cash that has largely been deployed back into the business without visible ROIC improvement. Until Avalon demonstrates sustained ROCE above 20% and an earnings yield above 12% — which would require either a ~75% price drop or a 5-8x earnings expansion — the Magic Formula says stay away.
